title: Competition Analysis
purpose: One-page competition section of a seed-stage investment memo. Explains how customers solve the problem today, why those approaches fail, how the market is organized, and where an investment-relevant wedge emerges. States plainly when the source materials do not support a thesis.
voice: A venture partner explaining a market to another investor. Customer workflow, market structure and investor insight come before product description. Plain, specific, declarative sentences; no hype words.

format.fit_rule: Render at the largest type scale between 1.16 and 0.76 that fits one page; shrink to fit as a last resort and warn the user.

source_line.empty_text: none in the materials; analyst view.

format.ref_convention: D<n> = primary deck slide/page n; S<k>.<n> = supporting document k, page n.

fields.label: One-line description
fields.instruction: What the company sells and to whom, in one plain sentence.

fields.label: Headline (investor takeaway)
fields.instruction: The investor takeaway in one sentence. If the evidence is thin, the headline says so.

layout.label: Evidence for the thesis
layout.style: Cream panel with a 3pt left border colored by rating

fields.label: Evidence for the thesis
fields.instruction: How well the sources support an investment thesis on competition and positioning.

fields.label: Why
fields.instruction: One or two sentences on why the thesis support is rated this way.

layout.title: How customers solve it today
layout.instruction: How customers solve the problem today: the actual workflow, who does it, what tools, people and vendors are involved, and where time, money or risk leaks out.

layout.title: Why those approaches fail
layout.instruction: Why those approaches fail, structurally (incentives, fragmentation, budget ownership, switching costs, distribution), not just 'they are inefficient'.

layout.title: The alternatives a customer weighs
layout.instruction: Ways customers solve this today, including the status quo. Name a specific company only if the sources name it; otherwise describe it by category.

columns.instruction: The alternative as a customer would name it.
Who relies on it and how.
The specific point where it fails the customer.

layout.title: Market structure
layout.instruction: How the market is organized: who holds budget, how buying happens, and why incumbents have not fixed the problem.

layout.title: Where the wedge emerges
layout.instruction: Where an investment-relevant wedge emerges and what has to be true for it to widen. If the sources do not support a wedge, say what is missing instead.

columns.title: What the materials do not show
columns.instruction: Specific things the sources do not show that the thesis needs.

columns.title: Questions for the founder
columns.instruction: Questions for the founder that would most change the view.

parts: Based solely on the uploaded materials.
Source references point to the slide or page the point is drawn from.

layout.pattern: [Company Name] Competition Analysis   [PAGE#]   Compiled on [DATE] by TEN Capital Network   [TEN Capital Logo]
layout.style: Open Sans 7pt, centered; logo TEN_Capital_logo_footer.png at 0.67in x 0.25in

evidence_record.shown_in: Evidence tab and <name>.evidence.json; not printed in the PDF

fields.instruction: One factual claim the analysis relies on.
Page refs where the claim is found.
Verbatim excerpt copied exactly from the cited page. Empty string for inferences.
